title: Show a settings file's description without its disabled settings

blocks.text: The admin console shows each settings file with its description on top: the block of comment lines a file opens with. Below it, the console lists the rest of the file, which it rewrites line for line when someone changes a value. Operators disable a setting by putting `#` in front of it, and since then the console shows `# smtp.debug=true` as part of a file's description, and a save drops the disabled settings from the file.

Write `description(...)` and `settings(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/SettingsFile.java`, using `comment(line)` to recognise a comment. The description is the comment block at the top of the file; the settings section is every line after it, in file order. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a file with a comment block and plain settings splits into the block and the settings
a file that starts with a setting has no description, and every line is a setting
a comment line further down the file is not part of the description
the settings section keeps the comment lines that sit among the settings, in place

origin.section: filter Keeps Every Match; takeWhile Stops at the First false

concepts: takeWhile returns the leading run of elements that pass and stops at the first false, and dropWhile returns the rest, so on input that is not ordered they differ from filter.
